resolution_rule: Resolve the complete predecessor state chain first, then add new_assessments below. Apply scope_updates and candidate_reconciliations without double-counting semantically identical source updates. No prior clean assessment is deleted or silently overwritten.

o_snapshot.delta: The two O commits since the previous comparator snapshot modify only agi/WORK_EXECUTION_STATE.json and finalize generation-13 recovery authority. The revision-22 action-adherence Execute request remains pending with no response, effect, scenario result or partial success claim, so no pending/configured/frozen work is promoted to evaluated evidence.

status_definitions.known: O explicitly encodes/discusses materially the same idea but no direct behavioral measurement of this clean mechanism/scope was found.
status_definitions.evaluated: O has direct explicit experiment/evidence on substantially the same mechanism under a named matched scope.
status_definitions.partially_tested: O measured or implemented a related adaptation/submechanism, but not the full clean mechanism or transfer scope.
status_definitions.uncovered: No materially equivalent O mechanism/direct test was found; generic adjacency is insufficient.

continual_learning.mechanism: Label/task-boundary-independent expert expansion from a distribution-distance threshold over recent latent memory, freezing prior ViT experts and using Dynamic Knowledge Fusion across components.
continual_learning.scope: Ye & Bors, Pattern Recognition 169 (2026), LEViT. Split MNIST/CIFAR10/CIFAR100 LEViT-DKF 96.81±1.37/51.74±1.23/23.03±1.32; Dynamic-CAA is 23.58±0.57 on CIFAR100. MiniImageNet 29.27±1.5. Reported component/parameter examples include 8/~11M, 6/~65M, 9/~97M; threshold gamma trades expansion count against accuracy and is dataset sensitive.

provenance.source: Ye & Bors, Online Task-Free Continual Learning via Expansible Vision Transformer, Pattern Recognition 169 (2026)

continual_learning.uncertainty: Vision/classification evidence; still recent-buffer dependent and capacity-growing. Same-label abrupt shift delay/false-expansion calibration is not reported.
continual_learning.o_comparison: O has source clocks/context invalidation and recursive optional routing, but no latent-distribution expert-expansion learner, frozen-expert ensemble, or matched LEViT-style continual-learning experiment.

continual_learning.mechanism: Boundary-free single-head continual structural adaptation by online creation/merge/prune of class-linked granular CNN structures, without image replay or explicit task-boundary detection.
continual_learning.scope: Leite, Neurocomputing 671 (2026). CIFAR10 Domain-IL strict single pass 85.52% versus 86.51% dense reference for one EfficientNet path; Intel-6 with two omitted classes 70.97% versus 61.87% standalone; SUN-397 combined Class/Domain-IL best 82.27% versus 80.74% without dynamic deferral and 60.12% offline reference.

provenance.source: Leite, Task-free continual learning with expansion-based granular CNN, Neurocomputing 671 (2026)

continual_learning.uncertainty: The strongest same-label Domain-IL stream is mild and this method avoids explicit boundary detection rather than measuring detection delay/false alarms; labels arrive after prediction.
continual_learning.o_comparison: O has no evolving granular classifier or boundary-free structural learner with matched continual-learning measurements.

cross_field.mechanism: Allocate stochastic evaluation budget from estimated gap-to-best and variance with a finite-budget correction, dynamically approaching OCBA as evidence/budget grows instead of equal allocation or premature winner concentration.
cross_field.scope: Cao et al., EJOR 2025 / arXiv:2304.02377v4. DAA versus OCBA PCS gains include +3.0pp at T=400 and +1.9pp at T=1000 in Example 1; +6.0/+5.6pp at T=1000/2000 in Example 3; +7.7/+12.4/+12.2pp at T=6000/20000/40000 in Example 4; smaller positive gains in facility-location and large-scale examples.

provenance.source: Cao et al., A Budget-Adaptive Allocation Rule for Optimal Computing Budget Allocation, EJOR 325(2), 2025

cross_field.uncertainty: Normal-sampling ranking-and-selection assumptions; plug-in gaps/variances can be unstable under nonstationarity/correlation/heavy tails. Reported gains are example-specific.
cross_field.o_comparison: O scores cost/information value and has scoped Candidate evaluation, but no variance/gap-based replication allocator, DAA/FAA target weights, or matched finite-budget PCS experiment.

cross_field.mechanism: Choose the next experiment to discriminate among currently plausible mechanistic models, update model/parameter uncertainty after each result, allow model-set revision, and retain an explicit cannot-discriminate/none-adequate state.
cross_field.scope: Kober et al., Chemical Engineering Research and Design 170 (2021). Real adsorption experiments; methyl-orange model discrimination was reported after five additional sequentially selected experiments, and another case caused revision of the rival-model set. No matched random/nonadaptive experiment count was recovered.

provenance.source: Kober et al., Sequential experimental designs for discrimination among adsorption equilibrium models, 2021

cross_field.uncertainty: Real-lab feasibility is strong, but no matched baseline speedup factor can be claimed from the accessible evidence; domain transfer is hypothetical.
cross_field.o_comparison: O values decision-changing information and falsifiable units, but no explicit rival-model posterior/discrimination experiment selector or model-set inadequacy state was found.

evaluation.mechanism: Accumulate sequential evidence at the highest plausibly independent experimental unit, aggregate by task/scenario cluster, and use cluster-aware covariance plus alpha spending rather than treating every record as independent.
evaluation.scope: Cluster-randomized sequential methods: 4/5 statistics reported satisfactory with as few as 10 clusters/arm. In 5,000-simulation clustered survival designs, representative O'Brien-Fleming type-I/power were .052/.808 fixed-cluster and .055/.814 variable-cluster; Pocock .048/.799 and .057/.800.

provenance.source: Zou et al. 2005; Li & Jung 2021/2022; Li 2020 clustered group-sequential evidence

evaluation.uncertainty: Clinical one-level cluster settings; agent evaluations may have nested step→trajectory→task dependence and few independent tasks. Post-hoc cluster-level choice may invalidate guarantees.
evaluation.o_comparison: O records every tool event and has evidence gates, but no cluster-robust sequential alpha-spending evaluator or task-cluster variance model.

evaluation.mechanism: Diagnose whether an interim statistic has the covariance structure required by independent-increment group-sequential boundaries; if not, construct stopping from the full joint covariance/information time.
evaluation.scope: Clustered survival and longitudinal GEE sources show independent increments can fail under cluster/within-subject correlation; covariance-aware designs recover roughly nominal operating characteristics in the tested settings.

provenance.source: Li & Jung 2021/2022; Shoben & Emerson 2014; Diao et al. 2025/2026

evaluation.uncertainty: A covariance diagnostic is a control mechanism, not a universal guarantee; finite-cluster and hierarchy-specific validation remains needed.
evaluation.o_comparison: O has no independent-increment diagnostic or full-covariance group-sequential evaluator.

evaluation.mechanism: Allow anytime-valid confidence-sequence/e-process stopping on dependent streams only when an explicit filtration-valid conditional-mgf/martingale condition is justified; otherwise re-unitize or use dependence-aware inference.
evaluation.scope: Howard et al. time-uniform Chernoff bounds establish time-uniform validity through nonnegative supermartingales under conditional structure rather than arbitrary dependence.

provenance.source: Howard et al., Time-uniform Chernoff bounds via nonnegative supermartingales, arXiv:1808.03204 / Annals lineage

evaluation.uncertainty: Structural statistical guarantee, not an agent benchmark gain. Adaptive policies, nonstationarity and correlated judge noise can violate the needed conditional assumptions.
evaluation.o_comparison: O has no e-process/confidence-sequence martingale-condition gate.

evaluation.mechanism: Drive interim evaluation by effective statistical information such as inverse cluster-aware variance rather than raw record fraction, because repeated records from one task can add much less information than a new independent task.
evaluation.scope: Diao/Li clustered sequential work derives covariance-aware information fractions. Karim 2026 repeated-record analysis: nominal 95% coverage row-level versus subject-clustered in a low-event setting falls .781/.887 at n=300, .742/.865 at n=1000, .617/.775 at n=5000; horizon-1 structural zero-covariance ablation gives .949/.949. Row-level SE was 26%-45% below subject-clustered as repeated records increased.

provenance.source: Diao et al.; Li & Jung; Karim 2026 sequential trial-emulation covariance study

evaluation.uncertainty: Karim is repeated-record variance evidence, not itself an optional-stopping guarantee; an agent-specific independent-unit mapping is unresolved.
evaluation.o_comparison: O counts events/traces and uses budgets, but no effective-information clock or hierarchy-aware variance accounting was found.

failure_evidence.mechanism: Agent benchmark results can be properties of the model×harness interaction rather than the model alone; freeze/disclose harness configuration and treat ranking as configuration-bound.
failure_evidence.scope: Zhang et al. 2026 preprint, fixed 100-task SWE-bench Verified subset, three models×three harnesses, two final runs/cell, same evaluator/50-step/120s-per-step budget. Harness ranges: GLM 13.0pp, GPT 8.5pp, Kimi 8.5pp; reported harness-induced variance 18.48pp² versus model-induced 2.37pp² (7.80x) and 6/9 model-pair×harness-pair ranking reversals. Raw final CSVs are not committed.

provenance.source: Zhang et al., Stop Comparing LLM Agents Without Disclosing the Harness, 2026-05-12

failure_evidence.uncertainty: Preprint/authors' table with public configs but incomplete raw-result reproducibility; 7.80x is not universal.
failure_evidence.o_comparison: O explicitly binds claims/evidence to exact executor/model/configuration/budget/conditions and forbids generalizing narrow results; the configuration-bound evaluation principle is known, though this harness grid was not reproduced.

failure_evidence.mechanism: Compare augmentation/memory/skill methods against a budget-aware strong vanilla control; equal nominal step count can confound claims when modules consume different total inference budgets.
failure_evidence.scope: Hajimiri et al. 2026 WebArena. Aggregate success means: Gemini Vanilla-IB 50.74 vs AWM44.98/ASI47.86/ReasoningBank45.54; GPT 36.63 vs30.74/32.14/28.42; Qwen47.44 vs43.58/45.61/43.09. Vanilla-IB is an approximate budget-aware control, not exact per-task token matching.

provenance.source: Hajimiri et al., Are Online Skill and Memory Modules Always Worth Their Tokens?, arXiv:2606.15017

failure_evidence.uncertainty: Specific WebArena/WorkArena methods/backbones and approximate budget matching; does not establish that memory/skills are generally useless.
failure_evidence.o_comparison: O Candidate evaluation explicitly considers baseline need, cost, risk and protected regression and Work Strategy optimizes elapsed time/information value, so the strong matched/budget-aware baseline principle is already known; these specific augmentation methods were not tested.

failure_evidence.mechanism: Persistent learned memory/skills can be contaminated when artifact admission is credited from final episode success rather than the correctness/contribution of the learned artifact itself; validate the artifact pathway separately from final outcome.
failure_evidence.scope: Same 2026 study. GPT Shopping ASI: 72.2% first-step induction failures, 54.2% of those recovered; AWM Shopping induction from ground-truth-failed trajectories 49.5% Gemini/52.3% GPT; ReasoningBank entries labeled successful but ground-truth failed 52.9%/59.5% in Shopping, with other domains also nonzero.

provenance.source: Hajimiri et al., arXiv:2606.15017 Appendix D

failure_evidence.uncertainty: Same study/implementations as FE-026; author diagnosis about missing intermediate judge evidence is not a randomized causal intervention.
failure_evidence.o_comparison: O separates Candidate applicability/evaluation from task PASS and preserves detailed action/tool evidence; successful final artifacts cannot erase policy violations. The artifact-vs-outcome admission principle is materially known, though no matched AWM/ASI/ReasoningBank contamination experiment exists.

long_horizon.mechanism: Recovery difficulty increases with downstream error-propagation depth; localize and resume from the earliest causally relevant conflict/error rather than waiting for a late visible failure or applying fixed-depth rollback.
long_horizon.scope: GUI-RobustEval/RoTS, ICML 2026 Spotlight: 1,216 recovery cases across 11 error types with injected depth d∈{0,1,3,5}; paper reports performance declining with depth. RoTS uses ~20k tasks/~800k synthesized items and reports RoTS-32B 47.4% OSWorld success and 33.8% All-Pass@4. Exact depth-wise cells were not primary-reverified in this worker run.

provenance.source: Recovering Policy-Induced Errors: Benchmarking and Trajectory Synthesis for Robust GUI Agents, arXiv:2605.29447

long_horizon.uncertainty: Supports causal/root-error localization but does not establish optimal checkpoint frequency/rewind policy; exact depth tables remain a primary-verification frontier.
long_horizon.o_comparison: O persists full action/tool traces, returns failed/uncertain tasks to fresh Root, and has checkpointed recovery/repair, so related recovery/localization substrate exists; it does not implement GUI state rewind or a depth-conditioned recovery policy/benchmark.

long_horizon.mechanism: Use millisecond-level stateful sandbox checkpoint/rollback to make branching/search/recovery cheap enough that checkpoint placement can become an explicit policy variable.
long_horizon.scope: DeltaBox 2026 reports approximately 14ms checkpoint latency and 5ms rollback latency on stateful-agent/SWE-bench/RL-style workloads; related systems work focuses on snapshot/restore latency. No controlled behavioral sweep of checkpoint cadence with success+recompute+storage+effect cost was found.

provenance.source: DeltaBox: Scaling Stateful AI Agents with Millisecond-Level Sandbox Checkpoint/Rollback, arXiv:2605.22781

long_horizon.uncertainty: Systems-overhead evidence only; low latency does not imply checkpoint-more-often improves behavior.
long_horizon.o_comparison: O has logical/durable checkpoints and immutable replay, but no sandbox snapshot/rollback primitive with DeltaBox-like latency or behavioral cadence experiment.

long_horizon.mechanism: Separate state rollback from external-effect safety using reversible/compensable effects, bufferable effects, and irreversible-gated effects; evaluate effect leaks/residue/concurrency separately from final task success.
long_horizon.scope: Atomix 2026. At τ-bench fault probability .30 transactional full mode reports 57% clean task success versus checkpoint-replay about 53%, described as statistically tied. Irreversible-send stress: 0/500 invalid sends leaked while all 500 valid sends were released; forced overlap reports zero conflict/invariant-violation witnesses for the transactional design.

provenance.source: Atomix: Timely, Transactional Tool Use for Reliable Agentic Workflows, arXiv:2602.14849

long_horizon.uncertainty: Pure task-success advantage is not cleanly established; compensation can leave semantic/cost residue and evidence is bounded to tested effects/workloads.
long_horizon.o_comparison: O already separates effect authorization from read-only observation, binds effects to manifests, rechecks revocations, uses idempotency and blocks network/publish inside model tools. Those are related effect-safety submechanisms, but O has no Atomix compensation taxonomy/transactional stress test.

multi_agent.mechanism: Treat pairwise evaluator noise as nonlinear near chance and condition filtering/escalation on whether errors are confidence-predictable rather than assuming one scalar verdict is reliable.
multi_agent.scope: Gao et al. arXiv:2404.09824 controlled preference-noise sweep 5%-50% in 5pp increments with 5-10 seeds. Below ~30% noise, +10pp noise generally costs <10 win-rate points; above ~40%, +10pp can cost 20-30 points; at 50% alignment is detrimental. Confidence filtering around 0.8 helps stochastic/Gaussian noise but not random flips.

provenance.source: Gao, Alon, Metzler, Impact of Preference Noise on the Alignment Performance of Generative Language Models, arXiv:2404.09824

multi_agent.uncertainty: DPO/alignment, not evolutionary search; ~40%-50% is an empirical danger region, not a universal search-collapse threshold.
multi_agent.o_comparison: O has objective/deterministic judges and uncertainty outcomes but no injected pairwise-judge-noise calibration or reliability-aware selection mechanism.

multi_agent.mechanism: Evolutionary search with noisy pairwise self-preferences using a Bayesian Bradley-Terry utility posterior, uncertainty-aware comparison allocation, order-swapped concordance checks, and confidence-aware pruning.
multi_agent.scope: Duel-Evolve 2026. MathBench final accuracy 94.0 versus Best-of-N 65.3; LiveCodeBench 37.4 versus 31.3. MathBench rises from ~57% to ~90% in the first 10 generations and 94% by generation 64.

provenance.source: Karlekar et al., Duel-Evolve: Reward-Free Test-Time Scaling via LLM Self-Preferences, arXiv:2602.21585

multi_agent.uncertainty: No known injected judge-error rate; systematic self-judge bias can survive repeated comparisons. Workshop evidence, specific benchmarks.
multi_agent.o_comparison: O has scoped Candidates but no Bradley-Terry pairwise population search, Thompson comparison allocation, or confidence pruning.

multi_agent.mechanism: Infer evaluator/annotator reliability with an EM-style latent reliability model and convert it to soft confidence weights instead of assuming all preference labels are equally trustworthy.
multi_agent.scope: RE-PO, ICLR 2026 / arXiv:2509.24159. Synthetic injected noise swept 0.0-0.8 and inferred reliability tracks the perturbed annotator; alignment examples include Mistral DPO 28.5/28.6 LC/WR to RE-DPO 35.5/33.0 and Llama-3 IPO 43.6/41.6 to RE-IPO 48.3/48.6.

provenance.source: Cao et al., RE-PO: Robust Enhanced Policy Optimization, ICLR 2026

multi_agent.uncertainty: Alignment-side rather than evolutionary archive-selection evidence; does not show search stability at 80% judge noise.
multi_agent.o_comparison: O records provenance/evidence classes but has no learned evaluator-reliability latent model or soft preference weighting.

multi_agent.mechanism: Use reversible Active/Standby/Terminated population states so temporarily low-value or uncertain agents can be reactivated when later information becomes useful rather than hard-pruned immediately.
multi_agent.scope: AgentRevive, ACL 2026. Reported +2.33% task-averaged performance and 15% token-overhead reduction. Llama3-8B full 68.53 vs w/o SEO66.01/w/o learned state policy62.80/w/o state message passing64.62; Qwen2.5-72B 84.34 vs81.86/80.21/81.09. Learned state policy is largest ablation loss.

provenance.source: Zhang et al., Taming Zombie Agents: A Markov State-Aware Framework for Resilient Multi-Agent Evolution, ACL 2026

multi_agent.uncertainty: At most five agents; no pure Standby-only versus hard-delete ablation holding all else fixed.
multi_agent.o_comparison: O's Candidate lifecycle is reversible, but it is not a learned multi-agent population controller with dormant/reactivation states; generic reversibility alone is not materially equivalent.

neuroscience.mechanism: Recurrent explicitly damped oscillatory AR(2)-equivalent nodes with fixed resonance frequencies and trainable cross-frequency coupling; golden-ratio-spaced frequencies as an inductive bias.
neuroscience.scope: Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023237 (2026). MNIST golden RRN .759±.007 vs LSTM .715±.019 vs standard RNN .617±.018; matched 11-node/252-param golden .759±.007 vs linear-spaced .592±.004, p=4e-14. Synthetic spike task .635±.001 vs .604/.575/.546; author reproduction notebooks public.

provenance.source: Kramer et al., Resonant Recurrent Network, Physical Review Research 8 (2026)

neuroscience.uncertainty: Modest supervised tasks; learning still uses BPTT and biological mapping is unproven; no independent third-party reproduction found.
neuroscience.o_comparison: O has no oscillatory recurrent network, learned cross-frequency coupling, or neural-weight training experiment.

neuroscience.mechanism: Replace dense recurrent transition with a circular local convolution initialized as a one-way shift so hidden-state information travels through a sparse wave-like buffer rather than being overwritten in place.
neuroscience.scope: Wave-RNN, ICLR 2024. Addition T=1000 iRNN MSE .16/unsolved within 60k vs wRNN ~6e-5/~2k iterations; psMNIST 96.7% vs tuned iRNN92.5; three-seed nsCIFAR10 54.70±.42 vs51.80±.54, though wRNN is below coRNN/LEM. Copy-task shift/sparse-conv ablations materially degrade performance.

provenance.source: Keller et al., Wave-RNN, ICLR 2024

neuroscience.uncertainty: Scope-specific; loses to iRNN on sMNIST and stronger recurrent baselines on nsCIFAR10; independent replication not yet audited.
neuroscience.o_comparison: O has no neural recurrent-memory architecture or wave-state training mechanism.

open_source.mechanism: Separate within-task failure repair from durable cross-task memory admission; require persistent memory to demonstrate held-out positive transfer against a no-memory/one-shot fallback instead of inheriting credit from better retry reasoning.
open_source.scope: Independent ReasoningBank SWE-bench Lite experiment, Claude Haiku 4.5, 30 instances×3 seeds. One-shot 45/90=50.0%; naive retry 38/90=42.2%; fresh per-instance bank 45/86=52.3%; persistent cross-task bank 21/45=46.7%. Persistent bank is -3.3pp vs one-shot and -5.6pp vs fresh in clean cells; arm3b is incomplete and raw cell bundle not committed.

provenance.source: ramankrishna/reasoning-bank independent SWE-bench Lite reproduction, 2026-05-31

open_source.uncertainty: Incomplete persistent arm (45/90 clean), highly bimodal 30-task pool, overlapping intervals and missing raw cell deposit. Does not refute original ReasoningBank.
open_source.o_comparison: O persists memory/procedure state and Episodes/Candidates across tasks and protects activation with held-out/regression/fallback machinery, so the transfer/admission submechanism is implemented but no fresh-vs-persistent ReasoningBank-style matched experiment is recorded.

reasoning.mechanism: Reuse a live elaborated proof-state snapshot across many tactic branches so branching cost is dominated by actual tactic/model work rather than repeated environment import and theorem re-elaboration.
reasoning.scope: Lean 4 snapshotting preprint arXiv:2605.25556, 45 prove-phase cases: 5.6-50x wall-clock speedup, average14x, median9.7x; fallback import+elaboration >99% of branch time in reported setup; snapshot path adds ~4-13s total overhead for a portfolio after one capture.

provenance.source: Keep the Proof State Live: Snapshotting for Efficient Tactic Search in Lean 4, 2026

reasoning.uncertainty: Small fixed tactic portfolio, one hardware profile and no learned branch selector; artifact reproducibility not confirmed in this run.
reasoning.o_comparison: O has restart-safe invocation reuse and checkpoint/recovery plus one exact bounded sibling-checkpoint experiment. That experiment rejected only width-3 checkpoint inheritance because invocations rose 1→3 for ~0.827s median wall-time improvement; this is related checkpoint reuse evidence, not a test of Lean proof-state snapshotting.

reasoning.mechanism: Dynamically route theorem-proving budget using proof-state similarity, compiler-error diversity and attempt history, stopping/restarting when predicted marginal value falls.
reasoning.scope: arXiv:2606.04883v3, 85 PutnamBench problems. Learned router reports 28.9% budget reduction at parity accuracy and +7.9% accuracy at parity cost. Feature ablations: all28.9, proof+error23.6, error+attempt20.3, proof+attempt19.7, attempt-only13.1. Noise-free oracle ceiling 62.0%.

provenance.source: Optimizing the Cost-Quality Tradeoff of Agentic Theorem Provers in Lean, arXiv:2606.04883v3

reasoning.uncertainty: Action space is only continue vs terminate/restart; proof domain and benchmark-specific; calibration beyond cost-quality curves remains open.
reasoning.o_comparison: O has strategy routing, recursive context selection and failure/retry boundaries, related implemented submechanisms, but no learned proof-success router or completed action-adherence result; the current revision-22 action-adherence Execute is still pending.

reasoning.mechanism: Diffusion-style iterative denoising/refinement of formal proof text with tactic-aligned masking as an alternative proof-search geometry.
reasoning.scope: Pythagoras-Prover 2026. MiniF2F-Test pass@32 diffusion4B 63.25% versus restricted autoregressive4B 74.6% and full autoregressive4B 86.1%; published diffusion setting uses 8192 generated tokens/8192 diffusion steps/block size8.

provenance.source: Pythagoras-Prover: Advancing Efficient Formal Proving via Augmented Lean Formalisation, arXiv:2606.12594

reasoning.uncertainty: Current controlled evidence is negative versus strong autoregressive generation; not compiler-feedback-guided repair and no general transfer claim.
reasoning.o_comparison: O has no diffusion generative model or proof-refinement decoder.

reasoning.mechanism: Use history-sensitive tactic-transition priors mined from successful proof sequences to rerank candidate tactics without replacing the base generator.
reasoning.scope: CoqGym study arXiv:2604.24354. Proved-theorem gains: ASTactic +5.64%, Tac +12.14%, Tok +9.24%, Passport +5.17%, average +8.05%; ~20% average unique added value in previously unproven theorems.

provenance.source: Understanding and Improving Automated Proof Synthesis for Interactive Theorem Provers, arXiv:2604.24354

reasoning.uncertainty: Coq rather than Lean; incremental value once semantic proof-state/compiler features exist is untested.
reasoning.o_comparison: O has no tactic generator, mined tactic-transition history prior or proof-search reranker.

scientist_agents.mechanism: Bind every reported quantitative result to a durable measurement registry/provenance record so manuscript claims cannot introduce unsupported numbers; keep provenance validity separate from experiment adequacy.
scientist_agents.scope: AutoResearchClaw 2026 best-of-3 component ablation over 10 topics. Full: completion10/10, selected quality5.62, accept3/10, no fabrication. Without Verification: completion10/10, apparent quality5.48, apparent accept5/10, but manual audit finds fabricated/unsupported measured values in 3/5 accepted papers. A semantically collapsed zero-valued experiment can still pass numeric grounding.

provenance.source: AutoResearchClaw: Self-Reinforcing Autonomous Research with Human-AI Collaboration, arXiv:2605.20025

scientist_agents.uncertainty: Small 10-topic best-of-3 system ablation; provenance prevents unlogged numbers but does not prove evidence adequacy or scientific validity.
scientist_agents.o_comparison: O binds artifacts, outcomes, observations, source versions and receipts with stable digests and refuses self-evaluation/internal tests as claim proof. Related provenance/admission machinery is implemented, but no AutoResearchClaw verification-gate ablation is reproduced.

scientist_agents.mechanism: Distinguish open stochastic semantic search from closed deterministic computation: re-explore open operators, and cache/merge only exact or explicitly certified-equivalent closed artifacts.
scientist_agents.scope: Eureka 2026 controlled suites: on 50,000 repeated-search tasks independent repeated open search succeeds 58.488% versus 24.492% when the first open-search output is forcibly memoized. On 30,000 adversarial surface-similar artifact pairs approximate semantic merging makes 100% false merges versus 0% for exact identity/certified equivalence; deterministic runtime optimizations change open-action ordering in 0/12,000 frontiers.

provenance.source: Eureka: Task-Conditioned Meta-Agent Orchestration for Scientific Discovery, arXiv:2608.19047

scientist_agents.uncertainty: Large but mostly synthetic/runtime suites from one report; real-discovery transfer and independent replication remain open.
scientist_agents.o_comparison: O deterministically reuses only exact completed invocation IDs/digests while meaningful semantic choices remain model/Candidate-controlled and frozen replay is exact. This is a closely related implemented open-vs-closed reuse boundary, but O has no matched Eureka memoization/semantic-merge ablation.

scientist_agents.mechanism: Make architecture/self-specialization evolution an amortized cost-benefit action gated by expected reuse and remaining horizon rather than always evolving, evolving only on stall, or complexity-triggered promotion.
scientist_agents.scope: Eureka 2026: governed evolution median cost/success2525.4/60.55% vs No Evolution2686.8/58.09%, Always Evolve3637.7/58.83%, Evolve on Stall2860.1/58.00%. EvolutionLease reduces median evolution round trips12→4 and control cost11.5%. Cost-aware lazy promotion reports 0.04% false promotion and median execution cost2277.13 vs complexity-only14.90% false promotion; cost-optimal reference2262.65.

provenance.source: Eureka: Task-Conditioned Meta-Agent Orchestration for Scientific Discovery, arXiv:2608.19047

scientist_agents.uncertainty: Controlled/synthetic task suites; no independent end-to-end scientific-discovery validation of the policy.
scientist_agents.o_comparison: O Candidate lifecycle explicitly evaluates applicability, baseline need, evidence, regressions, rollback, cost and risk and Work Strategy selects by expected elapsed-time/information value. That is related gated evolution machinery, but O has no horizon/reuse-amortization policy or matched always/stall/gated evolution experiment.

self_improvement.mechanism: Measure persistent-state self-improvement through explicit mechanism stages—plan-time consultation, structured rendering, procedure substrate, retrieval-before-action, and closeout—and test non-additive interactions across memory/procedural/update axes.
self_improvement.scope: PAST-Bench 2026: 26 task-family scenarios/204 episodes with fresh sessions and matched persistence on/off. Baseline Hermes overall persistence-on .66 with gap+.13. Isolated retrieval gate E4 gives best reported overall gap+.17; full Hermes+ overall gap+.15 while persistence-on remains .66. Full-minus-one procedural ablations show interactions, including removing E2 improving procedural reuse and removing E5 reducing it.

provenance.source: PAST-Bench 2026 persistence-pathway experiments

self_improvement.uncertainty: Three-run aggregate gaps have material variance; mechanism evidence is pathway-consistent, not causal necessity. Full stack is not proven universally better.
self_improvement.o_comparison: O persists memory/procedure state, has source consultation/optional routing/action binding/closeout-like receipts, and exact-scope Candidate activation. These are related persistence/routing submechanisms, but O has no matched persistence-on/off stage ablation.

self_improvement.mechanism: Evolve both task agents and an editable meta-improver while preserving an open-ended archive of stepping-stone agents; use learned meta-level machinery that can transfer to a new domain.
self_improvement.scope: DGM-Hyperagents 2026 after100 iterations: paper-review full .710 vs DGM-custom .590, w/o self-improve .0, w/o open-ended exploration .0; robotics full .372 vs .348/.213/.116. Cross-domain transferred fixed meta agent moved to Olympiad math yields best .630 after50 iterations versus initial meta-agent control .0, reported significant p<.05.

self_improvement.uncertainty: Compound ablations do not isolate individual memory/performance-tracking edits; parent selection remains handcrafted and cross-domain result is one target protocol.
self_improvement.o_comparison: O has reversible Candidates and retained evidence but no editable meta-agent evolution plus open-ended population/archive mechanism or matched cross-domain meta-transfer experiment. Generic Candidate storage is not equivalent.

scope_updates.update: ARROW public code narrows the causal claim: the long-term buffer uses iid random-priority retention (approximately a uniform history subset), whole minibatches come from one selected sub-buffer, replay also seeds actor/critic imagined rollouts, and the published ratio jointly changes storage allocation and sampling probability. No identical dual-buffer model-free control isolates a world-model-only causal effect; no independent reproduction was found.

Primary Cao et al. tables now quantify finite-budget DAA/FAA behavior. The prior guardrail should be represented as continuous plug-in gap/variance weighting rather than a hard global T switch; strongest extracted DAA-vs-OCBA PCS differences are setting-specific, up to +12.4pp in the reported examples.

A 2026 active dual GP-MPC numerical study supplies negative boundary evidence against unconditional probing: active versus passive steady-state error is 0.19% versus 0.17% at 5s and both 0.13% at 10s. Preserve information-value gating rather than treating active exploration as always beneficial.

LongDS-Bench now adds a controlled reset result: resetting once can improve low/medium-quality persistent trajectories but substantially harms high-quality persistent trajectories; reset gain is negatively correlated with persistent-state quality. Recovery should estimate both corruption and preservation value rather than treating fresh reset as universally safer.

Argus code tracing strengthens mechanical durability: reviewer verdicts can mark done, pause for operator, trigger bounded replanning, roll back premature stage progression and gate learned-candidate promotion. Important correction: independent Reviewer routing is conditional/policy-dependent, not universal; 466/731 SWE-Bench Pro trajectories used external review, and routing was not randomized.

Memento public parametric-CBR code exposes additional contamination mechanisms: memory case labels come from an LLM judge, the final query outcome truth_label is broadcast to every retrieved case for retriever training, and planner history persists across queries. These are implementation-grounded hypotheses, not proven causes of the reported negative-transfer cell.

AutoResearchClaw independently supports runtime repair without proving SAGE-specific multi-hypothesis diagnosis: removing Self-Healing reduces completion 10/10→6/10 and selected quality5.62→4.83; removing Debate+Self-Healing yields4/10 completion, quality3.47, zero accepted.

MLReplicate resource-text correction: the abstract's 38-fold input-token wording is inconsistent with detailed values (8.1K vs6.80M ≈840x); ~38.5x matches monetary cost $17.72/$0.46. Preserve detailed resource values and do not repeat 38x as a token ratio.

ACRA raw benchmark_translation.xlsx and Figures.ipynb were located, but exact critique-agent metric cells remain unreadable through the binary-limited path; qualitative ablation remains, with no guessed figure values.

HSI scope is strengthened: BabyAI/Crafter/TextWorld/MiniHack/NLE meta-on incremental effects over meta-off are +4.0/+8.2/+19.0/+10.0/+0.2; held-out BabaIsAI transfer is strong but meta-on is not uniformly superior to meta-off. Crafter development reward peaks before the last iteration, reinforcing non-monotonic best-version selection.

Bounded independent RHI reproduction: H0 .6014, H1 .6653, H2 .5986, static high-effort .6910; paired H1-H0 +.0639 95% CI[+.0222,+.1049], H2-H0 -.0028, H2-static -.0924. Forced structural growth H2-H0 -.1958; forward/reverse judge agreement only12/48 and11/48 in reported comparisons. Scope differs materially from the original RHI study and does not refute it.

candidate_reconciliations.reason: The same DeepSeek-V4-Flash HSI meta-on/meta-off mechanism and main 18.9→33.1→41.4 evidence was already represented in canonical C3. The new checkpoint adds held-out BabaIsAI detail and non-monotonic iteration scope but does not create a materially distinct semantic mechanism.

The bounded RHI reproduction is another source-bound instance of C8's multi-round self-evolution selection/revision-depth reliability mechanism: H1 can improve while H2 regresses, judge ordering is unstable, and structural growth is not monotonic. Preserve it as scope/evidence on C8 rather than double-counting a new mechanism.
